fixes.explanation: Close, but the money part is where this one slips. Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet in Judah, says the opposite: "I have neither lent nor borrowed, yet everyone curses me." (Jeremiah 15:10) So the cursing isn't about a loan. That's a rough deal, friend.

That's right, baker. Jeremiah says he has "…neither lent nor borrowed…" and still everyone curses him. (Jeremiah 15:10) No loan in the picture, and the cursing comes anyway. I think that's what stings.
Yes, baker. The LORD says He will enslave them to their enemies "…in a land you do not know…" (Jeremiah 15:14) That's the place He names for it. It's a heavy line, and it's okay to say so.

That's not the wording, friend. The LORD says the land is one "…you do not know…" (Jeremiah 15:14) Not knowing the land is the phrase the text uses. Read that line once more and the answer jumps right out.
That sounds gentle, but it isn't what Jeremiah asks. His prayer to the LORD is, "Avenge me against my persecutors." (Jeremiah 15:15) He says it plainly. Forgiving them isn't in that line.
Yes, baker. Jeremiah says, "Your words were found, and I ate them." (Jeremiah 15:16) Words taken in, not set aside. I think he treats them like something he needed.

Not quite, friend. Jeremiah, the prophet, is the one speaking: "Your words were found, and I ate them." (Jeremiah 15:16) Hide something and it ends up in the back of a junk drawer, and I lived in one for years. This verse has no drawer in it, just words taken in.

That's right, baker. Jeremiah says, "Your words became my joy and my heart’s delight." (Jeremiah 15:16) There's no heavy burden in that line. Joy and delight are what he names, even in a chapter full of trouble.

You got it, baker. Jeremiah says, "I never sat with the band of revelers, nor did I celebrate with them." (Jeremiah 15:17) The revelers are the group he names. He says he didn't sit with them or celebrate with them.

Close, but the text doesn't name them here. Jeremiah says, "I never sat with the band of revelers, nor did I celebrate with them." (Jeremiah 15:17) The group he names is the revelers. He says he didn't sit or celebrate with them.

Good guess, friend, but the elders aren't in this verse. Jeremiah says he never sat with "…the band of revelers…" (Jeremiah 15:17) Elders show up all over the Bible, but this verse names revelers. Read it again and you'll spot them fast.

That's a good-sounding job, friend, but I'd hand that gavel to somebody else. The LORD says, "…you will be My spokesman." (Jeremiah 15:19) A judge decides, and a spokesman speaks for Someone else. The verse names the second job.

That one's true, friend. The text says, "It is they who must turn to you, but you must not turn to them." (Jeremiah 15:19) The LORD says the people must turn to Jeremiah, and Jeremiah must not turn to them. Check the order of those words and it clicks.
Good guess, but cedar isn't in this verse. The LORD says, "…a fortified wall of bronze…" (Jeremiah 15:20) Cedar's a lovely wood, but the LORD names a metal. Bronze is the word.

I see the thinking, but the text says the reverse. The LORD says, "they will fight against you but will not overcome you…" (Jeremiah 15:20) So the fighting is named right there. The promise is that they will not overcome him.
That's right, baker. The LORD says, "they will fight against you but will not overcome you…" (Jeremiah 15:20) He says they will fight against Jeremiah. The promise is that they will not overcome him.
